A 2025 first-round draft pick, Simmons made eight starts as a rookie last season. He missed four games in midseason for a personal matter and then missed the last five games after going on IR following a wrist injury. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has started at left tackle in Simmons' absence. --Field Level Media

item.title: Lamar Jackson hits practice field, Ravens like chances of return
item.description: Lamar Jackson walked onto the practice field with teammates on Thursday with plans to participate as he works his way back from injuring his ankle on Oct. 4 against the Tennessee Titans.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lamar Jackson walked onto the practice field with teammates on Thursday with plans to participate as he works his way back from injuring his ankle on Oct. 4 against the Tennessee Titans. The two-time MVP quarterback missed two games -- a Baltimore win at Atlanta and last week's loss in Cleveland -- recovering from the injury. He last played in the first half of the Ravens' Week 4 win over the Titans. "Any time he's out there, it kind of elevates the whole group. We're certainly excited about the direction that he's heading," Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said Thursday. "He's still got a lot of work to do in order to be able to play on Sunday, but he's really working at it behind the scenes. It's great having him in the meeting room. And it's another thing to be able to have him out there on the field with us and continuing to push and his teammates seeing him push and all that stuff." Jackson has six TD passes and one interception plus a rushing touchdown in 14 total quarters played in 2026. In his stead, Baltimore turned to Tyler Huntley at quarterback. Even with a much-improved defense, the Bengals -- Sunday's opponent -- are not a team likely to be thrilled to see Jackson on the field. He's 11-2 as a starter against Cincinnati with 3,699 total yards (2,868 passing) and 26 TDs (two rushing TDs). "Tyler's played a lot of games for them over the years, done a really good job," Bengals coach Zac Taylor said. "I don't think anybody replaces Lamar, just one for one. But Tyler does a great job where I don't feel like they have to change anything that they're really doing. He can still make plays with his feet, he's made a lot of plays with his arm. He's smart, he understands their system. I think he's played really well for them over the years." Both Baltimore quarterbacks planned to take reps with the first team on Thursday in preparation for Sunday's game. The Ravens are one of three 4-2 teams in the AFC North and lead the division in points (156) while ranking last in points allowed (132). Baltimore has 116 points and 14 touchdowns with Jackson at quarterback this season, compared to 40 points and four touchdowns without him. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ex-prosecutor’s killing puts Guatemala’s crime-politics nexus back in focus
item.description: Former Guatemalan anti-corruption prosecutor Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa was one of the country's most high profile voices denouncing alleged links between politicians and business leaders and the country's increasingly powerful organized crime groups.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Menchu, Diego Oré
item.content:encoded: Former Guatemalan anti-corruption prosecutor Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa was one of the country's most high profile voices denouncing alleged links between politicians and business leaders and the country's increasingly powerful organized crime groups. Over the weekend, [USN:L6N46307D TEXT:"he was shot dead"] on a soccer field, a killing that former officials and diplomats consulted by Reuters said has heightened concerns over organized crime's influence in the Central American nation. The killing of an outspoken former prosecutor who had publicly challenged powerful interests shocked the country and revived debate over criminal networks’ penetration of state institutions. "This is a threat against human rights defenders. This is a threat against activists for democracy," said Frank La Rue, a human rights advocate, who attended the wake for Solorzano Foppa on Monday, which featured portraits of the slain lawyer with his family. For many Guatemalans, it recalled the 1998 assassination of Bishop Juan Jose Gerardi, beaten to death two days after presenting a report documenting atrocities from the country’s civil war, and stirred fears that violence could again be used against prominent critics of powerful interests. Experts said criminal networks have strengthened their influence in recent years as anti-corruption efforts and institutions tasked with combating impunity have weakened, issues likely to loom over the June 2027 election as Guatemala chooses President Bernardo Arevalo’s successor. Authorities have not established a motive for Solorzano Foppa's killing. But officials and diplomats said the case has fueled concerns about criminal groups’ ability to intimidate or silence critical voices. More than 100 former prosecutors, judges, journalists and human rights defenders have left Guatemala in recent years, according to some international human rights organizations, after denouncing corruption or alleged links between state structures and criminal networks. This week, following Solorzano Foppa's killing, a high-profile lawyer who also railed against political corruption said he has received death threats. On Wednesday, Arevalo denounced the threats against the lawyer, Edgar Ortiz. "Guatemala cannot return to being a country where defending democracy can cost one peace, freedom, or their life," Arevalo wrote on social media. 'RED LINE CROSSED' Corruption has been a major institutional challenge in Guatemala for decades. From 2007 to 2019, the UN-backed International Commission against Impunity in Guatemala (CICIG) helped investigate corruption and organized crime networks within the state, including cases that led to the resignation and subsequent prosecution of then-President Otto Perez Molina and his former vice president, Roxana Baldetti. Since CICIG's departure in 2019, human rights groups, prosecutors and international observers have denounced setbacks in the fight against corruption. President Arevalo, who took office in 2024 promising to tackle the problem, has acknowledged difficulties advancing reforms and dismantling structures accused of corruption. In videos posted on Facebook, TikTok and Instagram, and seen by Reuters, Solorzano Foppa alleged links between Barrio 18 leader Aldo "El Lobo" Ochoa, who is serving combined prison sentences of more than 1,600 years, and people close to the leadership of the National Unity of Hope (UNE) party, headed by former first lady Sandra Torres. Reuters could not independently verify the allegations. UNE told Reuters in a statement that "those allegations were never proven and should not be presented as established facts." Solorzano Foppa, a former head of Guatemala's SAT tax administration agency, also alleged ties between criminal networks, political figures and sectors of the judicial system, though the accusations did not result in judicial proceedings. Officials have not identified who ordered the killing. The Organization of American States and the United Nations have called for a thorough investigation. The Public Prosecutor's Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. On Sunday, following the murder, it said in a statement that "in order to guarantee due process, it will not disclose additional details about the evidence gathered or the specific lines of investigation." A former government official, who was not authorized to speak publicly, said insiders had turned to Solorzano Foppa with information they felt unable to expose themselves, making him an outlet for allegations from within the state. His killers "left no trace," the former official said, complicating the investigation. Guatemala's criminal networks range from gangs and drug traffickers to structures involving former officials and members of the security forces. Analysts say some have retained influence over state institutions, while armed groups like Barrio 18 and Mara Salvatrucha (MS-13) remain involved in extortion and territorial control. They include the so-called CIACS, or Illegal Clandestine Security Apparatuses, networks linked to former security structures that experts say retain political and economic influence. Guatemala is also a major drug-trafficking corridor to the United States, with groups associated with Mexico's Sinaloa Cartel and Jalisco New Generation Cartel operating through local criminal networks. "Many of us fear that a red line has been crossed," said Stephen McFarland, former US ambassador to Guatemala from 2008 to 2011. "A return to political assassination as a way of settling scores and protecting the ambitions and money of certain people."

item.title: Egypt calls for Yemen talks as parliament weighs military support to Saudi Arabia
item.description: Egypt advocates exploring "every opportunity" to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically, its foreign minister said, ahead of a parliamentary vote next week on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Egypt advocates exploring "every opportunity" to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically, its foreign minister said, ahead of a parliamentary vote next week on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis. Any direct involvement of the Egyptian military, one of the region's largest, would raise the stakes in the conflict between the kingdom and the Houthis, an increasingly destabilising front in the spreading US-Israeli war on Iran . President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Saturday for an urgent parliamentary session to authorise military involvement supporting the kingdom. After a closed session on Sunday, lawmakers [USN:S8N44Y029 TEXT:"postponed the vote until October 26"] to allow more deliberation. Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday to deliver a letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt's support would be [USN:S8N45S05P TEXT:"limited to defending Saudi territory"] and borders rather than attacking Yemen. What kind of support Egypt will ultimately provide remains unclear. EGYPT HAS LIMITED ROLE IN SAUDI-LED YEMEN COALITION Abdelatty said on Thursday that Egypt underlined the need to "explore every opportunity for the possibility of reaching political solutions" ensuring a full Houthi withdrawal from territory seized during the group's advance in September near [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"the Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] — a critical chokepoint at the Red Sea's mouth and gateway to Egypt's Suez Canal. "So that we can move on the political path that we always emphasize, and also side by side in support of the defensive path for the kingdom," Abdelatty told a press conference. Clashes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognized government have intensified since the group's push towards Bab el-Mandeb on the Red Sea further strained global oil supplies. The militia has since [USN:S8N44908G TEXT:"attacked Saudi airports and oil facilities"]. Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, is a vital strategic and economic partner for Egypt, providing billions in aid, central bank deposits and energy supplies under Sisi. The war in Yemen, which has caused a humanitarian crisis, started in 2014 when the Houthis drove the internationally recognised government out of the northern capital, drawing Saudi-led military intervention. Egypt joined the Saudi-led coalition in March 2015 mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes while pledging air support. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but played only a limited combat role. A US-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted attacks. While Cairo has voiced support for Riyadh since the resumption of hostilities, it has avoided direct combat. It did not join the Mecca mutual defense pact linking Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, though it says membership remains under consideration. The Saudi crown prince [USN:P8N3ZN0LL TEXT:"sought military assistance from the United States"], but President Donald Trump did not agree to the US striking Houthis, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters in September. Washington told Riyadh that it would help with intelligence sharing and targeting, they added. Yahya Ali al-Rai, speaker of the Houthi-run House of Representatives, warned on Saturday against Egyptian involvement, urging parliament to reject the proposal. "Should Egypt slide down this path, it would pose a grave threat to its own national security and internal stability," he said.

item.title: Presidente da Romênia pede segurança a crianças após dois ataques violentos a escolas
item.description: O presidente romeno, Nicusor Dan, pediu ao governo nesta quinta-feira que garanta a segurança das crianças nas salas de aula e na internet, após dois ataques violentos em escolas em menos de uma semana.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente romeno, Nicusor Dan, pediu ao governo nesta quinta-feira que garanta a segurança das crianças nas salas de aula e na internet, após dois ataques violentos em escolas em menos de uma semana. A polícia informou que um adolescente de 15 anos atacou dois colegas de classe com um facão nesta quinta-feira em um banheiro de sua escola de ensino médio na cidade de Pitesti, na região central da Romênia. Na segunda-feira, um estudante de 13 anos esfaqueou e feriu um professor e outro aluno. A mídia local informou que ele havia feito publicações sobre seus planos nas redes sociais pouco antes do ataque. “Dois sinais que não podemos mais nos dar ao luxo de ignorar”, disse Dan em uma postagem no X. “Precisamos de escolas mais seguras, professores apoiados e preparados para intervir, acesso real a aconselhamento psicológico, mas também medidas para a proteção de menores no uso do espaço online”, acrescentou o presidente centrista. O governo recém-empossado da Romênia realizará uma reunião na sexta-feira para discutir medidas de segurança nas escolas. As escolas na Europa enfrentaram uma série de ataques neste ano em países como Polônia, França e Suécia, com as autoridades, em alguns casos, apontando o papel das redes sociais e das subculturas online que glorificam o assassinato como fator que fomenta a violência.

item.title: É falso que Flávio Bolsonaro tenha dito que férias de 30 dias são "exagero"
item.description: O candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) não afirmou que férias de 30 dias são "um exagero", como dizem publicações nas redes sociais.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: O candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) não afirmou que férias de 30 dias são "um exagero", como dizem publicações nas redes sociais. Estes são os principais detalhes: “Flávio: 'Trinta dias de férias é um exagero. Quinze dias é mais do que o suficiente'”, alegam os posts, que circulam no Facebook e no Instagram com uma foto do candidato. A imagem tem o logotipo da Jovem Pan News, mas não há registro da suposta notícia nos perfis da emissora no Instagram , no Facebook e no X . Além disso, a fonte usada nos posts é diferente da utilizada pela Jovem Pan News. O plano de governo de Flávio apresentado ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) não menciona diminuir férias. “O custo de um trabalhador formal chega a cerca de duas vezes o salário que ele leva para casa... Vamos reduzir gradualmente o custo do trabalho, sem retirar direitos”, diz o documento. A Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT) assegura 30 dias de férias, sem prejuízo à remuneração, a cada ano de vigência do contrato de trabalho. A assessoria do candidato não havia respondido a um pedido de comentário até a publicação deste texto. Veredicto: Falso. Flávio Bolsonaro não disse que 30 dias de férias são um “exagero”, e a Jovem Pan News não publicou uma notícia com esta afirmação. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: Macron endurece restrições a protestos na França e culpa extrema-esquerda pelos distúrbios
item.description: O presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que protestos “ilegítimos” seriam proibidos nos próximos dias e atribuiu a culpa aos grupos de extrema-esquerda “sediciosos” e aos vândalos pelos distúrbios e saques ocorridos no último fim de semana.
item.dc:creator: Michel Rose
item.content:encoded: O presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que protestos “ilegítimos” seriam proibidos nos próximos dias e atribuiu a culpa aos grupos de extrema-esquerda “sediciosos” e aos vândalos pelos distúrbios e saques ocorridos no último fim de semana. Após uma reunião com chefes de inteligência e ministros de alto escalão, Macron afirmou que manifestações organizadas por grupos como sindicatos teriam permissão para ocorrer, mas poderiam ser redirecionadas por percursos alternativos para proteger as lojas. “No último sábado, tivemos atos políticos e sediciosos por parte de grupos de extrema-esquerda cujo objetivo é derrubar a República”, disse ele. Seus comentários foram feitos enquanto as autoridades em toda a França se preparavam para novos protestos, após alguns dos piores distúrbios urbanos do país nos últimos anos. O ministro da Justiça, Gérald Darmanin, disse que deseja a suspensão do direito de voto para pessoas que desrespeitem as proibições de participação em manifestações, bem como restrições ao acesso às redes sociais para pessoas envolvidas em violência, saques ou ataques à polícia. Todos os protestos planejados para sábado em Marselha e Lyon, a segunda e a terceira maiores cidades da França, foram proibidos, informaram as autoridades locais. No entanto, novas manifestações já estão se organizando antes do que as autoridades temem que possa ser mais um fim de semana conturbado. A principal união estudantil da França, a Unef, convocou manifestações para sábado, enquanto o movimento dos Coletes Amarelos, força antissistema que surgiu em 2018, apresentou planos para uma marcha pelo centro de Paris. Comerciantes no centro de Paris começaram a proteger as vitrines de suas lojas com tábuas, em caso de violência. O grupo de artigos de luxo Hermès informou que reforçou as medidas de segurança em suas lojas na França. Os organizadores da feira internacional de colecionadores de arte Art Basel Paris, realizada em um centro de exposições no centro de Paris, informaram que o evento ficará fechado durante todo o fim de semana. Em outro local, as autoridades da cidade de Orléans, no norte do país, se preparavam para possíveis distúrbios, já que a extrema-direita, representada pelo Reunião Nacional, realizaria uma reunião anual, enquanto sindicatos e grupos de esquerda planejavam manifestações. Um protesto estudantil convocado para quinta-feira em Paris foi inicialmente proibido, mas acabou sendo autorizado a ocorrer; no entanto, as estações de metrô no centro de Paris foram fechadas pelas autoridades de transporte público em antecipação a aglomerações não autorizadas. INDIGNAÇÃO PÚBLICA A França foi abalada em 17 de outubro por atos de violência à margem dos protestos em todo o país, expondo a profundidade da indignação pública e levantando dúvidas sobre a capacidade dos serviços de segurança de manter a ordem. Duas pessoas foram presas por um incêndio criminoso na prefeitura de Limoges, segundo autoridades francesas e a mídia. A terceira noite consecutiva de toques de recolher locais transcorreu sem incidentes graves nas áreas afetadas pela violência, proporcionando ao governo um certo alívio antes do fim de semana. A agitação revelou um mal-estar mais profundo na França, onde os custos crescentes da energia, a pressão sobre o orçamento familiar e as preocupações com a deterioração dos serviços públicos têm alimentado uma frustração crescente entre os trabalhadores e os jovens. A classe política francesa também mergulhou em uma acirrada troca de acusações, com o governo acusando grupos políticos de extrema-esquerda de alimentar a agitação. Destacando o mal-estar dos investidores, o prêmio de risco da dívida pública francesa em relação aos títulos alemães, considerados refúgios seguros, ampliou-se nesta quinta-feira para o maior nível em 15 anos, enquanto o rendimento do título de referência francês de 10 anos atingiu 5,14%, seu nível mais alto desde julho de 2002.

item.title: Canadian dollar extends daily winning streak as interest rate spreads narrow
item.description: The Canadian dollar strengthened to a one-month high against its US counterpart on Thursday as oil prices rose and the gap narrowed between US and Canadian interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: The Canadian dollar strengthened to a one-month high against its US counterpart on Thursday as oil prices rose and the gap narrowed between US and Canadian interest rates. The loonie was trading 0.3% higher at 1.4007 per US dollar, or 71.39 US cents, its strongest intraday level since September 21 and putting the currency on course for the sixth straight day of gains. The daily winning streak would be the longest since April. "Most importantly for the currency, the repricing of the Bank of Canada outlook has narrowed the two-year US-Canada yield spread," said Kevin Ford, an FX & macro strategist at Convera. "That has reduced the US dollar’s rate advantage at the same time that elevated oil prices have supported Canada’s terms of trade." The gap between Canada's 2-year yield and the equivalent US rate narrowed by 11 basis points to about 141 basis points in favor of the US note. Concerns about the sustainability of the AI outlook resurfaced, boosting the [USN:L6N468126 TEXT:"safe-haven appeal"] of US Treasuries. The price of [USN:L1N46801N TEXT:"oil"], one of Canada's major exports, rose after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns of further disruption to energy supplies from the key exporting region. US crude oil futures were trading 2.2% higher at $99.26 a barrel. "The USD-CAD is looking to test the 1.40 level on the downside, but extending the move below that threshold will likely require further support from Canadian data and the Bank of Canada," Ford said. Investors see a roughly 75% chance the Bank of Canada will raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% next Wednesday. Bets on a hike have increased in recent days after hawkish comments from BoC Governor Tiff Macklem and evidence of rising expectations for long-term inflation. Canadian retail sales data for August is due on Friday — analysts expect sales to rebound 1.3% after they declined 0.7% in July. Canadian government bonds tracked the moves in US Treasuries. The 10-year yield was down 7.8 basis points at 3.787%.

item.title: Estado de Rhode Island processa Meta por suposta tolerância a anúncios fraudulentos
item.description: O estado de Rhode Island, nos Estados Unidos, processou a Meta nesta quinta-feira em um tribunal estadual, devido à suposta tolerância da empresa à publicidade fraudulenta generalizada em suas plataformas Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O estado de Rhode Island, nos Estados Unidos, processou a Meta (META.O) nesta quinta-feira em um tribunal estadual, devido à suposta tolerância da empresa à publicidade fraudulenta generalizada em suas plataformas Facebook, Instagram e WhatsApp. O processo, movido pelo Procurador-Geral de Rhode Island, Peter Neronha, no Tribunal Superior de Providence, acusa a Meta de lucrar ilegalmente e participar da criação de bilhões de dólares em publicidade fraudulenta – mesmo enquanto assegurava a seus bilhões de usuários que estava trabalhando diligentemente para protegê-los. Este é o primeiro caso relacionado a golpes desse tipo movido contra a Meta por um estado dos EUA, após uma ação semelhante apresentada em maio pelo Condado de Santa Clara, na Califórnia. O processo busca indenizações civis monetárias por cada uma das supostas violações da lei estadual de Rhode Island cometidas pela Meta, restituição aos consumidores, devolução dos lucros ilícitos e uma ordem judicial que obrigue a empresa a lidar com os anúncios fraudulentos que desenvolve e veicula em suas plataformas, em vez de lucrar com eles. "Conforme alegado, Meta expôs conscientemente usuários vulneráveis a fraudes e golpes, obtendo lucros enormes com isso. Quando empresas, grandes ou pequenas, se aproveitam dos consumidores de Rhode Island, este escritório fará tudo ao seu alcance para responsabilizá-las", disse Neronha em um comunicado à imprensa. O processo cita reportagem da Reuters do ano passado sobre documentos internos da meta que detalham a vasta escala de publicidade fraudulenta nas plataformas da empresa – e os cálculos da Meta de que estava lucrando muito mais com anúncios fraudulentos de alto risco do que esperava pagar em multas por permiti-los. De acordo com esses documentos, a Meta exibe cerca de 15 bilhões de anúncios fraudulentos de "alto risco" para os usuários todos os dias e obteve aproximadamente 10% de sua receita de 2024 com comércio eletrônico fraudulento, produtos de saúde duvidosos e outros tipos de marketing proibidos. Em muitos casos, a ação judicial de Rhode Island alegou que as ferramentas de criação de anúncios com IA da Meta ajudaram ativamente os golpistas em suas práticas de marketing fraudulentas. Em vez de bloquear consistentemente os anunciantes que seus sistemas automatizados de detecção suspeitavam de fraude, Rhode Island alegou que a meta às vezes cobrava deles um valor extra como penalidade. "A Meta ajudou conscientemente a criar e otimizar esses anúncios para garantir que fossem o mais eficazes possível e, em seguida, mentiu sobre eles, deturpando para o público seu compromisso de prevenir fraudes em suas plataformas", afirmou o processo. A Meta não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário sobre o caso. A empresa contestou a reportagem da Reuters. "Combatemos agressivamente fraudes e golpes porque as pessoas em nossas plataformas não querem esse tipo de conteúdo, os anunciantes legítimos não o querem e nós também não", disse Andy Stone, porta-voz da Meta, em resposta à reportagem do ano passado, classificando-a como "uma visão seletiva que distorce a abordagem da Meta em relação a fraudes e golpes". Nos meses que se seguiram à publicação das reportagens da Reuters, a Meta alegou ter feito progressos em suas iniciativas de combate a golpes. No entanto, Rhode Island afirmou que os golpes continuam desenfreados e facilmente encontrados na biblioteca de anúncios da empresa, um banco de dados de anúncios veiculados nas plataformas da Meta. "O anúncio abaixo, por exemplo, prometia reverter Alzheimer em 45 dias", afirmou a denúncia de Rhode Island sobre um conjunto de anúncios fraudulentos. "Havia mais de 2.000 versões desse anúncio ativas na biblioteca de Meta Ads." COM FOCO NO PÚBLICO IDOSO Segundo apurou o estado de Rhode Island, os anúncios fraudulentos frequentemente tinham como alvo pessoas idosas, citando uma investigação do Centro para o Combate ao Ódio Digital (Center for Countering Digital Hate), uma organização sem fins lucrativos que identificou quase 94.000 anúncios fraudulentos nas plataformas da Meta. "Alguns desses anunciantes gastaram mais em anúncios da Meta ao longo de vários anos do que grandes marcas como Walmart ou Pfizer", afirmou o processo. Além dos golpes, o gabinete do procurador-geral de Rhode Island afirmou ter constatado que a Meta também estava falhando em fiscalizar outros tipos de anúncios ilícitos, como os de aplicativos de IA para pornografia deepfake. Em um exemplo fornecido pelo estado, um anúncio mostrava imagens lado a lado de uma mulher totalmente vestida em uma cafeteria, ao lado de uma imagem dela praticando um ato sexual. Rhode Island também citou exemplos de anúncios fraudulentos que se fazem passar por figuras públicas e instituições confiáveis, como bancos, para tirar proveito de sua credibilidade, incluindo um caso em que golpistas na China usaram o nome e a imagem de um alto executivo do Bank of America em anúncios no Facebook e Instagram que atraíam usuários para negociações fraudulentas de ações no WhatsApp. Dados de pesquisas públicas citados por Rhode Island – e avaliações internas da Meta obtidas pela Reuters – indicam que as plataformas da empresa são responsáveis por uma parcela desproporcional de golpes online e que as defesas da meta contra golpes eram mais fracas do que as de seus principais concorrentes em publicidade digital. "É mais fácil anunciar golpes em plataformas Meta do que no Google", concluiu uma análise interna da Meta em abril de 2025. Apesar disso, a Meta tentou frustrar os esforços regulatórios para exigir verificação, afirmou Rhode Island. O processo alegava que "um anunciante banido pode reaparecer no tempo necessário para fornecer um novo endereço de email ou número de telefone". (Por Jeff Horwitz e Katie Paul)

item.title: ECB's Santos Pereira pushes for deeper EU integration
item.description: ECB policymaker Alvaro Santos Pereira said on Thursday that Europe's difficult geopolitical environment and technological shortcomings show it is time to give fresh momentum to European integration by deepening the single market in services, transport and energy.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ECB policymaker Alvaro Santos Pereira said on Thursday that Europe's difficult geopolitical environment and technological shortcomings show it is time to give fresh momentum to European integration by deepening the single market in services, transport and energy. The remarks by Portugal's central bank governor add to growing calls from European policymakers to deepen integration and remove barriers seen as weighing on the bloc's competitiveness and growth. The single market reduced many forms of fragmentation, he noted, but significant barriers persist. The remaining challenges are more complex because they are rooted in national institutions and regulations, he said at a conference. It was vital to complete integration in areas where it remains limited, including services, transport and energy, he added.

item.title: Paraguay's central bank under pressure over politically connected lender
item.description: Paraguay's central bank and its president face mounting calls to resign as scrutiny intensifies over how they supervised a fast-growing digital bank with political ties.
item.dc:creator: Daniela Desantis
item.content:encoded: Paraguay's central bank and its president face mounting calls to resign as scrutiny intensifies over how they supervised a fast-growing digital bank with political ties. Senators from the ruling party and the opposition have urged President Santiago Peña to remove the central bank's top leadership, despite it being credited with helping [USN:S0N3ZU04S TEXT:"Paraguay"] secure investment-grade status. The case is testing the reputation that has helped Paraguay become one of South America's emerging destinations for foreign capital, much of it from neighboring Brazil. In recent weeks, authorities have repeatedly tried to calm financial markets after it emerged that ueno bank faced regulatory scrutiny of its business and an administrative investigation. The bank uses lower case in company statements. In written statements to Reuters, Paraguay's central bank defended its governance structure, saying regulatory and supervisory processes operate independently and in accordance with established legal procedures. Ueno said it would continue to "fully cooperate" with the central bank and maintained that the preliminary administrative proceeding did not constitute a finding of wrongdoing. Ueno has scaled rapidly from a niche local fintech player to a mid-tier bank, in line with digital platforms like [USN:L6N45I01U TEXT:"Monzo"] and [USN:S0N44O08P TEXT:"Nubank"]. It says it has 3 million customers and manages roughly $800 million to $850 million in public funds. Details of the preliminary probe appeared in a central bank report sent to the Senate this month. The report aimed to dispel doubts about loans issued by ueno to related companies, but it ended up fueling more questions from lawmakers, the banking association and other business groups. "The replacement of the Central Bank authorities must take place," ruling-party Senator Gustavo Leite said in an interview with Reuters. "The people at the Central Bank have lost credibility." Opposition Senator Rafael Filizzola said the financial system was "suffering" and filed another request for information on ueno, which experienced a major selloff of its global bonds. Fitch Ratings changed the outlook on the company's securities from stable to negative last week. Paraguay's Banking Association, which represents 14 private lenders including Brazil's Itau [RIC:RIC:ITUPU.UL], published a statement on October 18 reiterating that the central bank's response to the senate was "incomplete." POLITICAL TIES The case is politically sensitive. Paraguay's central bank president, Carlos Carvallo, previously worked at ueno and served as its president until August 2023, the company confirmed in a statement to Reuters. Peña, a former [USN:L4N3K813R TEXT:"economist"], was a business partner of the group that owned the bank until March 2025. Ueno said Peña never had a relationship with the bank itself as a shareholder or investor. Much of the pressure for answers has come from lawmakers of the ruling Colorado Party, amid an internal dispute over the party's presidential nomination for the 2028 general elections. In a written response to Reuters, the central bank said there was no conflict of interest, saying Carvallo had "recused himself" from all decisions related to ueno bank. Paraguay’s presidency did not respond to a request for comment. In remarks to local media in early October, Peña described the situation as an "overflow" of a technical matter that was taken into the political arena and had done "tremendous damage to the image of the entire country." The ueno case has put a spotlight on stability in Paraguay's grain-exporting economy that won investment-grade credit ratings from Moody's in 2024 and S&P Global last year. The IMF expects growth of 4.5% this year, almost double the [USN:L6N46117N TEXT:"regional average"].

item.title: Zelenski afirma que aún no se ha restablecido velocidad de Starlink, espera hablar con Marco Rubio
item.description: El presidente Volodimir Zelenski afirmó el jueves que aún no se ha restablecido la velocidad de Starlink en Ucrania, y añadió que espera mantener conversaciones con el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, en los próximos días.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente Volodimir Zelenski afirmó el jueves que aún no se ha restablecido la velocidad de Starlink en Ucrania, y añadió que espera mantener conversaciones con el secretario de Estado de Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, en los próximos días. Zelenski señaló que Ucrania está dispuesta a participar en conversaciones de paz durante la cumbre del G20 en Estados Unidos, pero que, hasta el momento, no se había recibido ninguna invitación al respecto. "Hay claramente una cuestión en juego: obligar a Rusia a poner fin a esta guerra", dijo el mandatario a periodistas en Kiev. "Es posible (...) con la mediación del presidente (Donald) Trump y de nuestros socios. Creo que todo es posible, y podemos contar con una reunión en Florida durante la cumbre del G20", agregó.

item.title: Why Anthropic is turning away some users
item.description: Bill Gross, founder of Idealab, is Silicon Valley’s idea guy.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: Bill Gross, founder of Idealab, is Silicon Valley’s idea guy. Over 30 years, he’s developed a methodology for spotting business ideas and used it to help start 175 companies through his incubator, with more than 45 exits. So it stung a little when, a few months ago, Gross found that AI had gotten disturbingly good at generating business ideas. He told me it left him feeling “depressed”. Then the feeling turned into an idea itself: what if he turned his methodology into a system anyone could use? That system, Idealab.ai , launched this week. It matches your background and skills against AI-generated business ideas, and lets you set the budget you’re willing to work with. Not every idea it spits out is going to be a great business, but Gross is betting the platform can lower the barrier to entrepreneurship for people who’d never otherwise know where to start. The human part, he insists, doesn’t go away. “All the judgment and decisions still have to be made by humans,” he told me. AI can offer suggestions, “but you have to make the call.” And, “you’ve got to be passionate about it, for sure.” OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L4N4661IU TEXT:"Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger is 'a good idea' as companies form deal committees"] [USN:FWN4661WE TEXT:"Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centers popular"] [USN:L6N46701V TEXT:"OpenAI says its AI agents weakened internal monitoring system"] [USN:L4N4660IQ TEXT:"Qualcomm to cut jobs worldwide in performance-focused layoffs, internal memo shows"] [USN:L6N4661EP TEXT:"SpaceX and Tesla's Terafab targets 2028 for volume chip production, Musk says"] [USN:L8N4650GT TEXT:"ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent place over $35 billion worth of Nvidia chip orders"] ANTHROPIC'S FIGHT WITH DISTILLATION Here’s a strange move for a company racing toward the largest IPO in history: turn away paying customers, on purpose, weeks before you go public. That’s effectively what Anthropic just did. Inside an investor meeting in San Francisco last week, my colleagues and I got a [USN:L6N4601AA TEXT:"behind-the-scenes look"] at how Anthropic’s executives are explaining a slowdown of their own making. The company has cut off a meaningful slice of paying customers — accounting for between 5% and 7% of its revenue in the first nine months of the year, investors at the meeting told us. The reasoning: those accounts weren’t typical customers. They were, Anthropic alleged, Chinese AI labs quietly mining Claude to train their own models. The technique is known as distillation in AI model development. A smaller “student” model learns by studying the outputs of a larger “teacher” model, essentially absorbing its capabilities secondhand. In February, [USN:L4N3ZJ1G1 TEXT:"Anthropic said"] Chinese labs including DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax had generated more than 16 million interactions with Claude through roughly 24,000 fake accounts, all in violation of its terms of service. Anthropic calls this more than a contract violation. It considers the practice a loss of intellectual property with national security implications. So the company rolled out new defenses earlier this month: applying access restrictions, proxy blocking, and bans on tens of thousands of accounts, which it says has cut off 90% to 99% of the data being siphoned. Anthropic is telling investors the crackdown has effectively stopped Chinese developers from distilling its models. Here’s why that matters for the IPO: it gives Anthropic a tidy explanation for something investors were already nervous about — a month-to-month growth deceleration. It may also address a bigger worry. Anthropic is betting that cutting off Chinese labs will slow their progress, not just stop a few bad actors from gaming the terms of service. The underlying numbers are still extraordinary by any standard. By this past March, Anthropic had already brought in $4.7 billion in a single quarter — more than all of 2025. Then it kept climbing: $11.6 billion in the second quarter, $16.8 billion in the third. But growth at that scale doesn’t usually keep compounding at the same rate forever. Competition from cheaper, open-source Chinese models remains one of the most common concerns investors are raising. Reuters has reported that [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"some investors are now discussing"] a valuation near $1.5 trillion for the IPO, down from the roughly $2 trillion once expected. The real question is whether this crackdown — and the short-term revenue hit that comes with it — actually buys Anthropic a lasting distance from its open-source rivals, or just a temporary edge. CHART OF THE WEEK According to [USN:L6N4650MN TEXT:"a new survey"] of more than 380 security and technology professionals by Salt Security, 86% of their organizations now have at least one AI agent operating, and 77% have agents chaining actions together across other agents. In other words, agents aren’t just answering questions anymore — they’re taking multi-step actions, often autonomously, deep inside company systems. What’s missing is the ability to actually watch them. Only 18% of those same organizations say they can automatically stop an agent that starts behaving unexpectedly, and just 13% can trace a complete path from instruction to outcome across every agent involved. That’s a massive visibility gap between how fast companies are deploying agents and how well they can monitor what those agents are actually doing.

item.title: The midterms reach Kyiv
item.description: US President Donald Trump has not so quietly shifted course on a major policy issue in the past month. After criticizing Russian President Vladimir Putin, he's started to make nice. What explains the turnabout? The November midterms may offer a clue.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has not so quietly shifted course on a major policy issue in the past month. After criticizing Russian President Vladimir Putin, he's started to make nice. What explains the turnabout? The November midterms may offer a clue. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, once Washington's most celebrated wartime ally, is finding himself caught in the crossfire of US midterm politics. He is under mounting pressure from Trump to strike a peace deal with Putin. With US voters increasingly frustrated by[USN:L6N45Z19G TEXT:" high energy prices"] and the cost of living, Trump has turned renewed attention to the war in Ukraine in recent days, arguing that a negotiated settlement there could help ease economic pressures at home, even though US consumers would be unlikely to feel the effects of any peace deal ahead of the November 3 vote. Trump has said the war may be closer than ever to finishing and that he wants the death and destruction to end. But he also may be betting that a resolution of the four-year conflict could ease pressures on the US economy, voters’ pocketbooks and his own political fortunes. Russia is a major oil supplier and has held out the possibility of a broad economic pact with Washington. In recent weeks, Trump has cut a deal with Putin, temporarily easing US sanctions on Russian diesel (and [USN:FWN4622VQ TEXT:"waiving others"]) in exchange for Moscow providing more diesel to global markets. He’s considering a [USN:SPN45Y0Z6 TEXT:"meeting with Putin"] and Chinese President Xi Jinping next month, without Zelenskiy. Meanwhile, Kyiv has [USN:P8N41Y023 TEXT:"complained that a satellite system"] made by US-based SpaceX has stopped working when mounted on fast-moving drones, limiting its ability to strike Russian targets and defend against attacks. The moves are a shift from Trump’s earlier [USN:S0N3S902L TEXT:"criticisms of Putin"] and a return to [USN:L2N3PI1I7 TEXT:"more prickly relations"] between the US and Ukrainian leaders. Ukraine and several European allies have expressed alarm at an apparent pivot by Trump. Trump has blamed [USN:L8N4620HY TEXT:"Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries"] for driving up global diesel prices. He’s also suggested that Ukraine needs a new leader. “Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine,” he told us at the White House on Monday. “Zelenskiy is not helping matters much.” Trump envoy Steve Witkoff later called Putin a “humanitarian” for [USN:L8N4670ON TEXT:"freeing a retired US schoolteacher"] in custody since 2022. The Ukrainian attacks have contributed to higher diesel prices, although market analysts attribute most of the increase to disruptions in fuel shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. That’s a consequence of a different war: the US-led one with Iran. Trump wouldn’t be the first politician to lay blame for inflation abroad. His Democratic predecessor, Joe Biden, [USN:L2N2VC04A TEXT:"pointed to Putin"] after Russia's invasion of Ukraine caused gasoline prices to surge ahead of congressional elections in 2022. Voters are not buying a similar argument from Trump. Some 78% of Americans say his policies bear at least some blame for rising prices, according to a [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"]. Most Republicans and Democrats cited the cost of living as their top concern. Zelenskiy told visiting US lawmakers on Monday that recent “decisions on the American side … are [USN:L4N4651HF TEXT:"hard to explain"].” For the answer, he may need to look no further than the US political calendar. TOP US POLITICS HEADLINES Special Report: Nine ways the Trump administration could interfere with the midterms Graphics: What redistricting means for Tennessee voters Podcast: Prediction markets and social good: An interview with Kalshi's CEO [USN:L4N4621CK TEXT:"As Trump's support slips, white evangelicals remain his Republican bedrock"] [USN:L1N4660O3 TEXT:"US Supreme Court rulings reshape midterm election battlefield"] [USN:L6N46108U TEXT:"High gas prices strain Detroit's hungry and food banks ahead of midterm elections"] POLL OF THE WEEK Your questions on election officials’ preparations for violent or legal threats How are election officials preparing for threats to poll workers, misinformation, administrative disruptions or attempts to interfere with voting and vote counting? Reuters interviewed more than 50 state and local election officials from both political parties, including a dozen secretaries of state, the top election officials in their states. Nearly all said they are adopting new strategies to prepare for political interference, misinformation, cyberattacks and even threats of violence ahead of the midterms. Their efforts span jurisdictions large and small, in areas controlled by Trump’s Republican Party as well as the opposition Democratic Party. In Michigan, for example, state officials are advising local clerks on the appropriate response if the federal government demands access to voting machines. Preparations fall into three categories. Some election officials are hiring lawyers or seeking legal skills, as over a dozen interviewees said. Twice that many election officials said they are expanding public outreach and social media campaigns to counter misinformation around the reliability of mail-in voting or voting machines. Most of the interviewed officials said they are scrambling to fill gaps left by the Trump administration’s cuts to programs that help safeguard elections from cyberattacks and physical security threats. That includes ongoing work to fortify election offices with camera systems and bulletproof glass – a trend that began after Trump disputed his loss to Biden in the 2020 election, prompting violent threats by Trump supporters against election workers . Read our reporting on more specific examples of what election officials are doing in preparation for such potential scenarios in Wisconsin, North Carolina, Georgia, Michigan, Colorado, and Maine. THE VIEW FROM PARIS The French government is bracing for the prospect of more protests as soon as this weekend after some of the [USN:L8N46401O TEXT:"worst urban tumult"] in years. Thousands were arrested, and shops looted, amid nationwide protests on October 17 over high prices and declining public services. Trump has weighed in repeatedly on the crisis, blaming immigrants and radical Islam for the violence, without providing evidence. In Kansas on Monday, Trump warned voters that the US would [USN:L1N4650ZT TEXT:"burn like France"] if Democrats win. Macron [USN:L8N4670KY TEXT:"shot back"] that Trump and other foreign leaders had spread misinformation about what happened and were looking to score political points at France's expense. He called comments by foreign leaders "stupid" and "unacceptable." WHAT TO WATCH FOR October 22: Trump rally in Sioux City, Iowa October 23: Trump rally in Fort Myers, Florida October 24: Trump rally in Perry, Georgia October 25: Trump rally in Port Huron, Michigan October 26: Trump rally in Corinth, Mississippi THE WHO, WHAT AND WHEN [USN:L1N4600WS TEXT:"The midterm election outcomes that could shape Trump's final two years"] [USN:L1N45N0R3 TEXT:"Six reasons Democrats may fall short of a midterm landslide in November"] [USN:L6N45Z1B9 TEXT:"Could disillusioned Kansas voters send their first Democrat to the US Senate in 94 years?"] [USN:L1N4660I0 TEXT:"How the Republican redistricting gambit faltered under Trump slump"]

item.title: US blocks two devices with Chinese-made surveillance chips
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it had blocked two devices from the US market that contain foreign surveillance chips produced by a subsidiary of China's Huawei, the first time it had exercised authority under new rules.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it had blocked two devices from the US market that contain foreign surveillance chips produced by a subsidiary of China's Huawei, the first time it had exercised authority under new rules. The US telecom agency said it barred a dashboard camera and a wireless video transmitter containing chips produced by Huawei subsidiary HiSilicon, which the agency said advertises its chip as "designed for the surveillance market" and including "detection algorithms for human faces." FCC Chair Brendan Carr said video devices containing surveillance chips produced by companies on its national security list "pose an obvious and unacceptable risk to the nation and our people." Huawei did not immediately respond to a request for comment and HiSilicon could not immediately be reached. The FCC voted in July to bar sales of devices in the US that contain key hardware from Chinese companies deemed to be national security risks The Trump administration has mounted a sweeping crackdown on Chinese technology gear

item.title: Romania to speed up development of Black Sea capabilities after cargo ship attacks
item.description: Romania will accelerate its development of surveillance capabilities and equipment to counter mines and drones in the Black Sea after a series of drone attacks on commercial ships off its coast, its top defence council said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Romania will accelerate its development of surveillance capabilities and equipment to counter mines and drones in the Black Sea after a series of drone attacks on commercial ships off its coast, its top defence council said on Thursday. At least [USN:L8N4610EC TEXT:"seven cargo ships"] have been hit near the coasts of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria in the past two weeks, with some 30 sailors reported dead or missing. Romanian F-16 fighter jet pilots [USN:L1N46306E TEXT:"shot down"] two of the latest generation of Russian drones over Romanian territorial waters on Saturday. [USN:L6N46613E TEXT:"NATO"] said on Tuesday it will send more maritime patrol aircraft, radar systems and drones to the Black Sea. Romania's top defence council said latest ship attacks are direct consequences of Russia's aggression beyond Ukraine's borders. Threats to freedom of navigation and critical energy projects in the Black Sea pose a security crisis for Romania. The current risks require concrete measures to protect human lives, maintain free access to national ports, and ensure the security of energy facilities in the Exclusive Economic Zone. The top defence council said it will accelerate the development of capabilities for maritime surveillance, countering naval mines and intervening against drones illegally breaching national airspace and waters. Authorities will practice to improve the efficiency of their operational response. Romania will seek to improve cooperation with fellow NATO members [USN:L8N43A0JZ TEXT:"Bulgaria and Turkey"] with whom it shares the Black Sea. "The Council members also analyzed ways to intensify coordination within NATO. This includes strengthening the deterrence and defense posture on the Eastern Flank and identifying new measures to respond to threats in the Black Sea region."

item.title: Nigeria says Ebola case remains isolated, urges calm
item.description: Nigeria's health minister said on Thursday authorities had no evidence that the country's recently confirmed Ebola case had spread into the wider community, describing it as a single, contained infection.
item.dc:creator: Camillus Eboh
item.content:encoded: Nigeria's health minister said on Thursday authorities had no evidence that the country's recently [USN:L6N4670RQ TEXT:"confirmed Ebola case"] had spread into the wider community, describing it as a single, contained infection. Nigeria reported its first Ebola case in more than a decade on Tuesday, becoming the fourth African country and the most populous yet to be affected by an outbreak that health officials have described as the [USN:L6N4421DF TEXT:"fastest-spreading on record"]. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said "there is no evidence that it has gone into the communities" and that there was "no need for any panic", as health officials intensified contact tracing and monitoring of people who may have been exposed "This is a contained, single case and we are diligently working to ensure that it remains so," he said Pate said there was no reason at present to alter plans for large public gatherings, but left open the possibility of additional measures if the situation worsened "We have only one case, and hopefully it will stay that way," he said

item.title: El STOXX 600 europeo sufre su mayor caída en tres semanas por desplome de bancos y alza del crudo
item.description: El índice europeo STOXX 600 anotó el jueves su mayor caída en tres semanas, lastrado por la debilidad de las acciones bancarias, mientras que el alza de los precios del petróleo y el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos franceses frenaron aún más el apetito por el riesgo.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: El índice europeo STOXX 600 anotó el jueves su mayor caída en tres semanas, lastrado por la debilidad de las acciones bancarias, mientras que el alza de los precios del petróleo y el aumento de los rendimientos de los bonos franceses frenaron aún más el apetito por el riesgo. * El índice paneuropeo (.STOXX) cerró con una caída superior al 1%, a 637,74 puntos. El índice bancario de la zona del euro (.SX7E) fue el de peor desempeño, con un descenso del 4,2%, lo que supuso su peor jornada desde marzo. * El español Bankinter (BKT.MC) cayó un 7,6% tras publicar sus resultados, que revelaron que el aumento de las tasas de interés incrementó los costos de los depósitos y ejerció presión sobre los márgenes en el tercer trimestre. * Barclays (BARC.L) cayó un 2,3% tras anunciar unos beneficios del tercer trimestre inferiores a lo esperado. El banco anunció que recortará este año unos 5.000 puestos de trabajo, lo que supone el 5% de su plantilla. * En general, los resultados empresariales europeos han sido sólidos, lo que en ocasiones ha ayudado a los inversionistas a hacer caso omiso de un panorama económico sombrío. Sin embargo, las caídas del jueves ponen de manifiesto lo rápido que puede deteriorarse la confianza cuando unos resultados decepcionantes chocan con la incertidumbre económica. * "Tenemos grandes preocupaciones en el mercado", dijo Joost van Leenders, estratega sénior de inversiones de Van Lanschot Kempen Investment Management, refiriéndose al conflicto de Oriente Medio que el jueves llevó a los futuros del crudo Brent a un máximo de cinco meses. * Además, el diferencial de rendimiento entre los bonos franceses a 10 años y los bonos alemanes (Bunds) también alcanzó un nuevo máximo de 15 años en un contexto de incertidumbre política y protestas en Francia. * Hermes (HRMS.PA) cayó un 5% después de que el fabricante de los bolsos Birkin publicó unos ingresos trimestrales ligeramente inferiores a lo esperado, lo que lastró el índice de lujo (.STXLUXP) . * Nestlé (NESN.S) subió un 1,1% tras anunciar un crecimiento orgánico de las ventas en el tercer trimestre mejor de lo esperado. El índice de alimentación y bebidas (.SX3P) subió un 0,6%, uno de los pocos sectores que cerró al alza. * El índice tecnológico (.SX8P) volvió a sufrir presiones, siguiendo la tendencia de ventas masivas en el mundo, y cerró con una caída del 2%. Las acciones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial, como Infineon (IFXGn.DE) , STMicroelectronics (STMPA.PA) y ASML (ASML.AS) , cayeron entre un 5% y un 6%.

item.title: トランプ氏、レブロン・ジェームズ選手を批判 国歌斉唱中に「無礼な振る舞い」
item.description: [２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２２日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２２日、米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のスーパースター、レブロン・ジェームズ選手が試合前の国歌斉唱中に「無礼な振る舞い」をしたとして批判した。

トランプ氏は自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」への投稿で「国歌を聴いている間、レブロン・ジェームズはわが国を侮辱する態度を取った」と述べ、ジェームズさんが国歌斉唱中に体を動かしている様子を映した動画を添付した。

さらに「レブロン・ジェームズは、米国国旗とわが国が象徴する全てのために命を捧げた偉大な米国の戦士や英雄たち全員に謝罪すべきだ！」と非難した。

トランプ氏が共有した動画には、ジェームズさんが所属するセブンティシクサーズの選手たちと一列に並び、ウオームアップとして腕を振ったり、シュートの動作をする様子が映っていた。

item.title: Penguins F Ben Kindel back in Pittsburgh after fainting on team plane
item.description: Penguins forward Ben Kindel is back in Pittsburgh after he was hospitalized in Salt Lake City and might even return to practice as soon as next week, general manager Kyle Dubas said Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Penguins forward Ben Kindel is back in Pittsburgh after he was hospitalized in Salt Lake City and might even return to practice as soon as next week, general manager Kyle Dubas said Thursday. Kindel, 19, had an urgent medical issue about 10 minutes after the team charter departed Salt Lake City International Airport on Tuesday, forcing the aircraft to turn around and land. Team medical staff cared for him until the plane was on the ground, at which time emergency medical technicians from a waiting ambulance took over. Dubas revealed that Kindel fainted due to a "vasovagal episode." He was given oxygen on the aircraft and regained consciousness. Formally called vasovagal syncope, it is "a common, generally benign type of fainting caused by a sudden drop in blood pressure and sometimes heart rate, which temporarily reduces blood flow to the brain," according to Johns Hopkins Medicine. It can be triggered by a variety of situations, including standing too long or prolonged exercise, per Johns Hopkins. "He's back in the building for treatment and testing today," Dubas said. "We'll place him on injured reserve and will obviously follow very strict guidelines to ensure a safe return to training and play for Ben. That's our primary goal." Doctors gave Kindel the OK to return to Pittsburgh on Wednesday. He was accompanied by the team staff members who remained in Utah with him. Pittsburgh was returning home from a four-game road trip that concluded Monday with a 5-4 loss to the Utah Mammoth. Kindel played 18:53 in the game and did not record a point. The 11th overall selection in the 2025 NHL Draft, Kindel is in his second season with Pittsburgh. He has two goals and two assists through nine games this season after totaling 17 goals and 18 assists in 77 games as a rookie. Kindel, a native of Coquitlam, British Columbia, made the Penguins out of training camp as an 18-year-old last season. Pittsburgh is scheduled to return to action Thursday when it hosts the Florida Panthers. --Field Level Media

item.title: Penguins, following positive news about Ben Kindel's condition, face off with Panthers
item.description: The Pittsburgh Penguins return to the ice against the visiting Florida Panthers on Thursday night, two days after a health scare involving Ben Kindel.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Penguins return to the ice against the visiting Florida Panthers on Thursday night, two days after a health scare involving Ben Kindel. The 19-year-old forward fainted on the team flight out of Salt Lake City on Tuesday. The flight returned to the airport, and Kindel was taken to the University of Utah Hospital for further evaluation. General manager Kyle Dubas said Thursday that Kindel suffered a case of vasovagal syncope. It is "a common, generally benign type of fainting caused by a sudden drop in blood pressure and sometimes heart rate, which temporarily reduces blood flow to the brain," according to Johns Hopkins Medicine. The Penguins canceled practice on Wednesday as they prepare to open a three-game homestand by hosting the Panthers, but they had to take the practice ice on Thursday with relief, knowing Kindel should be able to return to practice soon. The Panthers likely aren't as happy after seeing their three-game winning streak end with a 5-1 road loss against the Ottawa Senators on Wednesday. Brady Tkachuk scored and Akira Schmid made 25 saves for Florida. Tkachuk spent his first eight seasons in Ottawa before requesting and receiving a trade this summer. In his return, he gave the Panthers a 1-0 lead 10 minutes into the game. Tkachuk has 11 points (seven goals, four assists) in his past five games, including two natural hat tricks. The Panthers had scored 18 goals over their previous three games. With Thursday being the second of back-to-back games, it could mark the NHL debut of Florida goalie Cooper Black, who was recalled from Charlotte of the AHL with Jacob Markstrom out 10 to 14 days with an upper-body injury. Black, a 25-year-old Dartmouth product, joined the Panthers organization as an undrafted free agent in 2024 and signed a two-year, two-way contract extension in June. "He'll get some games," Panthers coach Paul Maurice said. "He's been good. He's been good in practice. He looks like he fits. He looks comfortable. It's the right time for him to get in." At 6-foot-8, Black will become the tallest starting goaltender in NHL history when he makes his debut. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, is in a 1-6-1 rut since winning its first two games of the season. The Penguins just concluded an 0-4-0 road trip. On Monday night in Utah, Pittsburgh rallied from a 5-2 deficit to get within 5-4 on Declan Carlile's goal at 14:55 of the third period. However, the Penguins could not get the equalizer as Kindel's point-blank attempt was saved by Sebastian Cossa in the final minute. Erik Karlsson and Rickard Rakell each had a goal and an assist for the Penguins, and Bryan Rust recorded two assists. Arturs Silovs made 24 saves. The Penguins had scored three goals or fewer in each of their previous seven games. "My viewpoint is that we're facing some adversity right now," Muse said. "We have to stay together. We have to just be looking to make gains here each day, definitely each game and we have to make the way we play on the defensive side a priority and consistent." Karlsson has six points (two goals, four assists) in a four-game point streak. Rust left the game in the second period due to a lower-body injury after crashing awkwardly into the boards. He didn't return to action and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, head coach Dan Muse said Thursday. The Penguins swept three games from the Panthers last season. Captain Sidney Crosby had two goals and an assist in a 5-3 win on Oct. 23 in Sunrise, Fla. Evgeni Malkin accounted for three goals and an assist in a 9-4 rout on April 4 in Pittsburgh, and Rakell scored two goals and Crosby collected a goal and two assists in a 5-2 win the next day in Pittsburgh. --Field Level Media

item.title: Índice europeu STOXX 600 sofre maior queda em 3 semanas, com bancos em queda e petróleo em alta
item.description: O índice europeu STOXX 600 registrou nesta quinta-feira sua maior queda em três semanas, pressionado pela desvalorização das ações bancárias, enquanto os preços mais altos do petróleo e o aumento dos rendimentos dos títulos franceses reduziram o apetite por risco.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: O índice europeu STOXX 600 registrou nesta quinta-feira sua maior queda em três semanas, pressionado pela desvalorização das ações bancárias, enquanto os preços mais altos do petróleo e o aumento dos rendimentos dos títulos franceses reduziram o apetite por risco. O índice pan-europeu fechou com queda de mais de 1%, a 637,74 pontos. O índice bancário da zona do euro (.SX7E) foi o que apresentou o pior desempenho, caindo 4,2% — seu pior dia desde março. O Bankinter da Espanha (BKT.MC) caiu 7,6% após divulgar resultados que mostraram que as taxas de juros mais altas aumentaram os custos com depósitos e pressionaram as margens no terceiro trimestre. O Barclays (BARC.L) caiu 2,3% após divulgar um lucro no terceiro trimestre abaixo do esperado. O banco informou que cortará cerca de 5.000 empregos, ou 5% de sua força de trabalho, ainda este ano. Os resultados corporativos europeus têm sido, em geral, sólidos, às vezes ajudando os investidores a ignorar um cenário econômico sombrio. As quedas nesta quinta-feira, no entanto, mostram com que rapidez o ânimo pode se deteriorar quando resultados decepcionantes se chocam com a incerteza econômica. O spread de rendimentos entre os títulos de 10 anos da França e os Bunds alemães marcou o maior nível em 15 anos em meio à incerteza política e aos protestos na França. “O aumento do spread entre os títulos soberanos franceses e os do restante da zona do euro provavelmente ainda vai se acentuar nos próximos meses”, escreveu Jonas Goltermann, economista-chefe de mercados da Capital Economics. A Hermes (HRMS.PA) caiu 5% depois que a fabricante da bolsa Birkin divulgou receita trimestral ligeiramente abaixo do esperado, com a queda pesando sobre o índice de luxo (.STXLUXP) . A Nestlé (NESN.S) subiu 1,1% após divulgar um crescimento orgânico das vendas no terceiro trimestre acima do esperado. O índice de alimentos e bebidas (.SX3P) registrou alta de 0,6%, sendo um dos poucos setores a encerrar o dia em alta. As ações do setor de saúde (.SXDP) foram as que mais valorizaram, com alta de 2,1%. O grupo biofarmacêutico belga UCB (UCB.BR) subiu 21,6% após elevar sua previsão de crescimento da receita para 2026. O índice de tecnologia (.SX8P) sofreu nova pressão, acompanhando uma onda global de vendas, e registrou queda de 2%. Ações relacionadas à IA, como Infineon (IFXGn.DE) , STMicroelectronics (STMPA.PA) e ASML (ASML.AS) , caíram entre 5% e 6%. Os sólidos resultados da Meta (META.O) divulgados na quarta-feira não foram suficientes para acalmar as preocupações dos investidores quanto à sustentabilidade e à lucratividade dos enormes gastos com IA, reacendendo preocupações que já haviam desencadeado várias ondas de vendas em ações do setor de IA neste ano. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) fechou em queda de 1,01%, a 637,95 pontos. Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) recuou 0,27%, a 10.723,56 pontos. Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) caiu 1,04%, a 25.379,49 pontos. Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) perdeu 1,42%, a 7.809,42 pontos. Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve desvalorização de 2,51%, a 48.395,36 pontos. Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou baixa de 1,98%, a 18.940,90 pontos. Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) desvalorizou-se 1,41%, a 9.241,93 pontos.

item.title: US railroads pull ahead as high fuel costs hit truckers harder
item.description: Record fuel prices are pushing freight off US highways and onto trains, helping railroad companies rake in higher revenue and profits as shippers look for cheaper ways to move goods long distances.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Gomes, Apratim Sarkar
item.content:encoded: Record fuel prices are pushing freight off US highways and onto trains, helping railroad companies rake in higher revenue and profits as shippers look for cheaper ways to move goods long distances. [USN:L4N46817V TEXT:"Union Pacific"] (UNP.N) , [USN:L4N4680RT TEXT:"Norfolk Southern"] (NSC.N) and [USN:L1N467138 TEXT:"CSX"] (CSX.O) all reported a jump in third-quarter profit and revenue this week, with company executives saying high fuel costs and fewer available trucks were sending more business their way. "Railroads are much more efficient. It costs us way less per ton to move products across the US. So when fuel prices go up, it's naturally an advantage," Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena told investors on a post-earnings call on Thursday. The shift gives railroads a chance to win back long-haul freight from trucks, though higher fuel prices are raising their own costs and squeezing margins as the Iran war keeps fuel prices elevated. Diesel, a key cost for freight carriers, [USN:L6N45N17X TEXT:"reached a record"] $6.53 per gallon in September, according to AAA data. Railroad gains are showing up most clearly in intermodal shipments, where freight is moved by rail for the long-haul portion of the journey, with trucks typically handling pickup and final delivery. Intermodal shipments compete directly with long-haul trucking. "We are seeing long-haul truckload shift to intermodal and increased use of transload and rail-served distribution centers," said James Mourafetis, head of transportation, logistics and services at consulting firm EFESO. Union Pacific's domestic intermodal volume rose 13% from a year earlier in the third quarter, while CSX reported a 7% rise and Norfolk Southern 3%. Shrinking trucking capacity is also moving some freight onto rail. A prolonged freight downturn has forced smaller carriers out of the market, with high operating costs and stricter driver enforcement limiting the return of trucking capacity. "The truck market has certainly flipped this year, but recent tonnage levels confirm this is due to reduced capacity, not robust demand," said American Trucking Associations' Chief Economist Bob Costello. However, higher fuel prices are also raising costs for railroads, making it harder to translate stronger revenue into higher profits, though fuel surcharges have offset some of that pressure. Union Pacific said high fuel prices hurt its third-quarter operating ratio by 140 basis points, while Norfolk Southern said fuel costs accounted for about half of the year-over-year increase in both revenue and expenses.

item.title: Top RFK Jr. adviser Calley Means quits Trump administration
item.description: Calley Means, a close aide to US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., is resigning from his role as a senior adviser in the Trump administration, he said in a post on X on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Calley Means, a close aide to US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., is resigning from his role as a senior adviser in the Trump administration, he said in a post on X on Thursday. Means, who has been particularly active in the Kennedy-led “Make America Healthy Again,” submitted his resignation to Kennedy on Wednesday, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters. "It was an honor to advocate for MAHA moms in the administration and steer policies like Dietary Guidelines reform, psychedelic reform, removing soda from SNAP, removing food dyes, GRAS reform, and overhauling government food procurement," Means said in his post on X. He added that he is resigning from the White House with "tremendous respect for President Trump and Bobby Kennedy." Means stepped into a [USN:L1N41D1B6 TEXT:"permanent role"] as senior adviser supporting food and nutrition policy in November last year. Before that, he served as an adviser in the Trump White House from March to October as a special government employee. The Wall Street Journal, which first reported his resignation earlier on Thursday, said Means was significantly frustrated by White House delays of some of Kennedy’s most popular policy ideas and blamed others in the administration for allowing food companies and special interests to have too much sway, citing people familiar with the matter. The Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. His sister, Casey Means, also a key ally of Health Secretary Kennedy, had her nomination for US surgeon general [USN:L1N41D1B6 TEXT:"withdrawn"] by President Donald Trump earlier this year.

item.title: Com apoio a Trump em queda, evangélicos brancos seguem como base sólida entre republicanos
item.description: O presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, está perdendo apoio entre muitos dos eleitores que o reelegeram para a Casa Branca em 2024. Mas pesquisas Reuters/Ipsos e entrevistas com cristãos evangélicos brancos mostram que eles continuam sendo seu eleitorado mais fiel e podem se revelar cruciais nas eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Layne, Julio-Cesar Chavez, Jason Lange
item.content:encoded: O presidente norte-americano, Donald Trump, está perdendo apoio entre muitos dos eleitores que o reelegeram para a Casa Branca em 2024. Mas pesquisas Reuters/Ipsos e entrevistas com cristãos evangélicos brancos mostram que eles continuam sendo seu eleitorado mais fiel e podem se revelar cruciais nas eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro. Com os republicanos na defensiva em meio a índices de aprovação de Trump em níveis historicamente baixos, uma forte participação dos evangélicos poderia ajudar o partido a limitar as perdas causadas pela frustração dos eleitores com o custo de vida e a guerra contra o Irã. Essa lealdade ficou evidente na semana passada na Village Church, uma congregação evangélica em Blythewood, na Carolina do Sul, onde centenas de fiéis se reuniram para o sermão semanal “Bíblia e Política”, ministrado pelo pastor Erik Estep. O pano de fundo: uma disputa inesperadamente acirrada por uma vaga no Senado dos EUA, atualmente ocupada por um republicano. Falando no salão principal de culto, emoldurado por uma tela gigante de vídeo e iluminação no estilo de show, Estep não endossou nenhum candidato ou partido. Mas, ao se pronunciar contra o jogo, após sermões sobre aborto e socialismo, ele exortou seus fiéis — predominantemente brancos — a enxergarem a política por uma lente bíblica. “Acredito que a igreja é o baluarte da verdade para nossa nação”, disse Estep do palco. “E serão necessárias pessoas como vocês e igrejas como esta para proteger esta nação espiritual e moralmente.” A mensagem ressoou em Karen Whiting, uma executiva aposentada do setor farmacêutico de 72 anos que planeja votar na republicana Darline Graham em vez de Annie Andrews, a democrata. Graham foi nomeada pelo governador para ocupar a vaga de seu falecido irmão, o senador Lindsey Graham. Whiting citou preocupações de que os democratas permitam que meninas e mulheres transgênero participem de esportes femininos, ecoando outros evangélicos brancos entrevistados pela Reuters na Carolina do Sul na semana passada, que priorizaram questões sociais e religiosas em detrimento das preocupações econômicas. Andrews, no entanto, afirmou em um anúncio de campanha recente que se opõe à participação de mulheres transgênero em esportes femininos e às cirurgias de afirmação de gênero para menores de idade. “Estou votando em favor dos princípios bíblicos e não acredito que o Partido Democrata defenda esses princípios”, disse Whiting. “Sem Deus, este país está fadado ao fracasso.” Se os presentes na Village Church precisassem de orientações mais explícitas sobre como votar, um guia de candidatos disponível no saguão da igreja não deixava dúvidas. Produzido pelo grupo conservador cristão Palmetto Family Council e distribuído a igrejas em toda a Carolina do Sul, o guia atribuiu a Graham marcas de verificação verdes em todas as sete questões avaliadas, incluindo restrições à medicação abortiva e aos cuidados de afirmação de gênero, enquanto Andrews recebeu principalmente Xs vermelhos. Em um sinal da crescente competitividade da disputa pelo Senado, Trump fez campanha por Graham em um comício na noite de quarta-feira na Universidade de Clemson, na Carolina do Sul, concentrando grande parte de suas críticas em questões transgênero e acusando falsamente Andrews de apoiar a “mutilação sexual” de crianças. Andrews apresentou uma interpretação diferente das prioridades dos eleitores evangélicos. Em declaração à Reuters, ela disse ter visitado igrejas evangélicas e se encontrado com eleitores de várias religiões, orientações políticas e origens, constatando que a principal preocupação deles era a economia. “Eles estão enfrentando dificuldades com o custo de tudo. É por isso que estou concorrendo”, afirmou ela. LAÇOS FORTES Pesquisas Reuters/Ipsos mostram que o apoio a Trump entre os evangélicos brancos caiu para 63% neste mês, ante 77% em janeiro de 2025. A queda é ligeiramente menor do que a observada entre o eleitorado como um todo, de 47% para 31%, e os evangélicos brancos continuam sendo o único grande grupo demográfico monitorado pela Reuters/Ipsos em que seu apoio ultrapassa 60%. O vínculo de Trump, que já se casou três vezes, com os evangélicos brancos resistiu a uma década de escândalos e investigações, incluindo dezenas de alegações de conduta sexual imprópria — que ele nega — e um caso de pagamento para silenciar uma atriz pornô. A questão para os republicanos é se as pressões econômicas e a insatisfação com a guerra contra o Irã, agora em seu oitavo mês, estão enfraquecendo esse vínculo. Entrevistas da Reuters com 15 pessoas em duas igrejas da Carolina do Sul sugeriram que sua influência sobre os eleitores evangélicos brancos continuava forte. Na Village Church e na Carolina Baptist Church, na cidade de Spartanburg, a cerca de 90 minutos de carro de Blythewood, apenas 2 das 15 pessoas disseram estar considerando votar em Andrews, e nenhuma indicou que estava abandonando Trump. Embora vários tenham expressado frustração com o conflito com o Irã e o aumento dos preços da gasolina, a maioria disse confiar que Trump impedirá o Irã de obter uma arma nuclear ou, assim como Trump, atribuiu a inflação às políticas adotadas pelo presidente democrata Joe Biden. Chad Connelly, um ativista evangélico que lidera o grupo cristão de engajamento eleitoral Faith Wins, disse que, embora os evangélicos “não gostem de pagar preços mais altos”, eles se mobilizam igualmente por questões sociais. As preocupações com atletas transgêneros estão “realmente presentes em todos os lugares” nas quase duas dúzias de Estados que ele visitou neste ciclo eleitoral, afirmou. A lealdade dos evangélicos brancos a Trump reflete o que Robert P. Jones, presidente do Public Religion Research Institute (PRRI) — uma organização sem fins lucrativos que estuda religião e política — chama de “grande acordo” forjado durante a eleição de 2016. Muitos evangélicos ignoraram sua conduta pessoal em troca de seu compromisso de restringir o aborto e os direitos LGBTQ, promover uma visão cristã conservadora da vida norte-americana e adotar políticas de imigração rígidas que alguns apoiadores veem como uma forma de preservar a identidade cristã branca do país, disse Jones. “Isso provou ser mais importante para esse grupo do que o que eles estão tendo que pagar no posto de gasolina”, disse Jones, que escreveu extensivamente sobre a ascensão do nacionalismo cristão na política norte-americana, à Reuters.
